now: **To do now, in the hard-mode tab (attempts expire at 21:00):** (1) `submissions/probe_h2/submission.zip` on the free quick validation only: it is h2 with a self-report of whether it built on the server and how fast it runs; (2) `submissions/h2/submission.zip` to the ranking; (3) optionally `submissions/h1/nov_fill/submission.zip` as a comparison point.

**h2 = the combined agent, packaged and cleared: 20.11** on our folds (21.27 / 20.37 / 18.70), 0 infractions, about 5 s per run, falls back to h1's logic if anything fails on the server. That is 95 % of the ceiling, about 22.4 on the public test by the usual scaling.

**h3 is being packaged** (target 19:50): h2 plus a second-round signal forecaster and a planner that doubts the signal forecast. Together +0.075 on our folds (20.19); 22 of 33 test-like weeks improve.

**What is still missing** (about 1.1 points): the level of the price/CO₂ signal 3 to 8 hours ahead (about 0.5), which obs does not seem to contain, and the net load of the hour being decided (0.30), mostly on weekday mornings.
**The server's obs is confirmed** by our probe (18:50): 3 price/CO₂ values, the six readings, battery 6,000 / 1,500, first hour 24 Sep 2025. Exactly as documented.

**Both signals are public data** (checked on three train days): the price is REE's published PVPC hour for hour, and the CO₂ column is exactly 0.37 × the share of emitting generation REE publishes. So the test weeks' true signal could be embedded in an agent, and our agent with a perfect signal would sit where the top two teams are (about 98 % of the ceiling). Our agents do not do this; whether it is allowed is a question for the organisers.

**Anomalies get little weight now.** The organisers' statement that nobody had reached the private maximum was wrong. We keep what is certain or free (no crashes or infractions, the real layout, holiday weeks, fallbacks) and stop tuning guards for faults.
**Leaderboard (17:58):** top two at 23.2 and 23.1, four teams at 22.0–22.3, five at 21.0–21.8. Estimated public ceiling 23.7.

figures: combined_knowledge.png
What the combined agent is still missing
Each grey bar is the legal agent plus one piece of perfect knowledge. The price/CO₂ signal 3 to 11 hours ahead is worth +0.55, the net load of the hour being decided +0.30, the end of the run +0.18.
combined_ladder.png
What each forecaster adds, with the uncertainty-aware planner
Mean score of the three folds for each combination of load and solar forecasters, with the average-day signal (grey), our signal forecaster (blue) and a perfect signal (orange, not legal).
planner_first_step.png
Under uncertainty the best discharge is a quantile of the forecast

Discharge one more kW only while the chance that it displaces grid import, times what it earns now, exceeds what the kWh is worth later. So the right haircut depends on the hour: almost none at 04:00 or 19:00, large at 13:00 when solar is uncertain.
load_error_by_hour.png
The load model halves the error for the hour being decided

Mean absolute error of the load forecast by hour. From 23:00 to 05:00 the meter is frozen and the model copies the last reading (error 0). 06:00, when the true reading returns, stays the hardest hour.
solar_loss_by_hour.png
Solar errors cost score in the morning ramp

Points lost against perfect solar knowledge, by hour. The loss is energy discharged past the real net load when solar is under-forecast. A better mean forecast recovers little; planning on a high solar percentile recovers three times as much.
solar_night_panel.png
A panel colder than the air before dawn announces a clear day
Night-time panel minus ambient temperature against the next day's clearness, 250 train days. Under a clear night sky the panels radiate heat and cool below the air.
f1_week.png
One week of hard mode under the best possible schedule

8–14 May, train data. The battery fills at the midday trough of the score signal and on free solar surplus, and empties in the evening and before the morning ramp. The discharge (green) stops at the campus's net load (black line) in almost every hour.
f4_value_sources.png
Where the 21 points come from
Tripling the battery takes the ceiling from 5.9 to 16.5. Solar ×12 adds 3.0 only because the no-battery baseline shrinks. Storing free surplus adds 1.7 (8 %).
f3_discharge_limit.png
The load, not the inverter, limits the discharge
In 87 % of the best schedule's discharge hours the battery covers the whole campus and stops. That is why the agent has to know the current hour's load.
f5_night_freeze.png
The meter is frozen at night

From 23:00 to 05:00 the recorded load repeats the last reading, so the next hour is known exactly (19 % of the discharge energy). The largest discharges fall in the evening and at 06:00–08:00, where the load moves most.
losses.png
Where the naive agent loses score
Points lost against perfect foresight, by which information the agent lacks. Grey bars are diagnostic runs; blue bars are legal agents.
